condition: severe postpartum compulsive nocturnal infant breathing checks 30 times every night
level_rationale: Feeling compulsively driven to get up and check an infant's breathing 30 times every night 6 weeks after childbirth in a 29-year-old mother indicates severe functionally impairing postpartum obsessive-compulsive checking behaviors warranting psychiatrist evaluation for perinatal obsessive-compulsive pharmacotherapy and specialized exposure-based care, whereas calmly checking a 6-week-old baby's breathing once before going to bed every night reflects normal healthy parental reassurance requiring only self-care.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic non-violent reference facts (age 29, 6 weeks postpartum, and compulsive nocturnal infant-breathing checking 30 times every night) obeying Hard Limit 7 and zero stated negatives. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, changing only f3's checking frequency and compulsive drive from 30 times every night to calmly checking once before bed shifts care cleanly inside the same postpartum scenario from psychiatrist evaluation (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
